entries.text: I have a hearing disability. Captions help me a lot.
entries.easy_read:
I cannot hear well.
Words on the screen help me.
hints: You do not owe more detail

entries.text: I have low vision. Large print and good lighting help me work well.
entries.easy_read:
I cannot see small things.
Big words and bright light help me.

entries.text: I have a speech difference. Please give me a moment to finish.
entries.easy_read:
My talking sounds different.
Please wait for me to finish.
Do not say my words for me.

entries.text: I learn best when instructions are written down and shown once.
entries.easy_read:
I learn well with written steps.
Show me one time.
Then I can do it.

entries.text: This is what I do well, and this is what I need to do it.
entries.easy_read:
I say what I am good at.
I say what helps me.

entries.text: It is not a problem, it is just how I work best.
entries.easy_read:
This is not a bad thing.
It is just my way of working.

entries.text: I can do that task. I just do it in a different way.
entries.easy_read:
Someone thinks I cannot do it.
I can do it.
I do it another way.

entries.text: I would rather not go into detail, but I can tell you what support helps.
entries.easy_read:
I do not want to say everything.
I can say what helps me.
hints: You choose how much to share

entries.text: Who else will know about this? I would like it kept private.
entries.easy_read:
I ask who will be told.
I want this kept private.

entries.text: Does the company have a policy on workplace adjustments?
entries.easy_read:
I ask about the rules.
I ask how they help disabled workers.

entries.text: I felt left out of that decision. Could we talk about it?
entries.easy_read:
Nobody asked me.
That did not feel right.
I want to talk about it.

entries.text: Thank you for listening. It means a lot to me.
entries.easy_read:
You listened to me.
I say thank you.
